definition: Corpus linguistics is an empirical method for the study of language by text corpus (plural corpora).
details: Corpora are balanced, often stratified collections of authentic, "real world", text of speech or writing that aim to represent a given linguistic variety. Today, corpora are generally machine-readable data collections. Corpus linguistics proposes that a reliable analysis of a language is more feasible with corpora collected in the field—the natural context ("realia") of that language—with minimal experimental interference. Large collections of text, though corpora may also be small in terms of running words, allow linguists to run quantitative analyses on linguistic concepts that may be difficult to test in a qualitative manner. The text-corpus method uses the body of texts in any natural language to derive the set of abstract rules which govern that language. Those results can be used to explore the relationships between that subject language and other languages which have undergone a similar analysis. The first such corpora were manually derived from source texts, but now that work is automated. Corpora have not only been used for linguistics research, they have been increasingly used to compile dictionaries (starting with The American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language

explainer.lead: Corpus linguistics studies language through collections of real speech or writing rather than relying only on intuition or invented examples. Counting patterns across these texts helps researchers describe how a language is actually used and compare it with other languages studied in the same way.

tiers.eli5: Imagine putting lots of real conversations and pieces of writing into a carefully chosen basket, then looking through them to see which words and patterns appear. That is the basic idea of corpus linguistics. The basket can be large or small, but it should fairly represent the kind of language you want to understand.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, build a machine-readable corpus from authentic speech or writing, with a balanced and often stratified sample representing the target linguistic variety. Use it for quantitative analysis of words or grammatical patterns, then interpret the results as evidence about that variety. A large text collection is not automatically a good corpus: poor balance and an unrepresentative sample can distort the analysis.
tiers.paperLevel: Corpus linguistics is an empirical method that derives descriptions of a natural language from a corpus: an authentic, balanced collection of speech or writing intended to represent a linguistic variety. Quantitative measurements over the corpus support analysis of linguistic concepts and comparison with other languages analysed similarly. Its evidential value depends on how well the corpus represents its target and on preserving natural language use with minimal experimental interference; corpora need not be large.

explainer.example: To study a particular variety of English, a researcher could assemble authentic samples of both speech and writing in deliberately balanced proportions. They could then count how often a grammatical pattern occurs in each part and compare the rates. Those measurements would provide evidence about its use in that variety, instead of relying only on examples invented by the researcher.

usedIn.name: Linguistic research
usedIn.detail: Researchers quantify linguistic patterns that would be difficult to test through qualitative analysis alone.

usedIn.name: Dictionary compilation
usedIn.detail: Corpora supply evidence from authentic language use for compiling dictionaries.

usedIn.name: Cross-language comparison
usedIn.detail: Languages analysed through comparable corpus methods can be examined for relationships between their described patterns.

explainer.intuition: A language can be described more reliably by examining many authentic examples in their natural context than by depending only on a researcher's judgments. The key is not merely collecting text, but collecting a sample that represents the linguistic variety being studied.
howItWorks: Choose the linguistic variety to investigate.
Collect authentic speech or writing from its natural context, with minimal experimental interference.
Build a balanced, often stratified corpus; the result is usually machine-readable and may be large or small.
Run quantitative analyses of words, structures, or other linguistic concepts.
Use the findings to derive language rules and, where comparable analyses exist, explore relationships with other languages.
explainer.whyItMatters: Corpora make language claims testable against authentic usage and permit quantitative analysis at scales that qualitative inspection cannot easily handle. They also provide empirical evidence for dictionaries, linguistic descriptions, and comparisons between languages.
misconceptions: A corpus is not just any large pile of text; it is designed to represent a particular linguistic variety.
Corpora do not have to be huge: some contain relatively few running words.
The method uses natural language data with minimal experimental interference, rather than requiring controlled experiments.
